title: The image of an idempotent endomorphism of a finite free module is finite projective and commutes with base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ and $p:R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus n}$ an $R$-linear map with $p\circ p=p$, with matrix $X\in M_n(R)$ in the standard basis. (i) $R^{\oplus n}=\operatorname{Im}(p)\oplus\operatorname{Im}(1-p)$ (internal direct sum, with $\operatorname{Im}(1-p)=\ker p$), so $\operatorname{Im}(p)$ is a finite projective $R$-module (a direct summand of a finite free module). (ii) Let $\rho:R\to S$ be a ring map and $p_S:S^{\oplus n}\to S^{\oplus n}$ the $S$-linear map with matrix $\rho(X)$ (entrywise); then $p_S\circ p_S=p_S$, and the $S$-linear map $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS\to S^{\oplus n}$, $v\otimes s\mapsto s\cdot\rho(v)$ ($\rho$ applied to coordinates), is injective with image $\operatorname{Im}(p_S)$; hence $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS\cong\operatorname{Im}(p_S)$ as $S$-modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module, line 2020), last sentences: 'is an idempotent element p which lifts p-bar. Setting P = Im(p) we win.' (that Im(p) is finite projective and that it lifts P-bar, i.e. that the image of an idempotent commutes with base change, is left to the reader there)

proof.text: Put $q=1-p$. Then $q^2=q$ and $pq=qp=0$, while $p+q=1$. Every $v\in R^{\oplus n}$ therefore has the decomposition $v=p(v)+q(v)$ with the two terms in $\operatorname{Im}(p)$ and $\operatorname{Im}(q)$. If a vector lies in both images, write it as $p(a)=q(b)$; applying $p$ gives the vector equal to $0$, so the sum is direct. Moreover $q(v)=v$ whenever $p(v)=0$, and $p(q(v))=0$, hence $\operatorname{Im}(q)=\ker(p)$. Thus $R^{\oplus n}=\operatorname{Im}(p)\oplus\operatorname{Im}(1-p)$, and the first summand is finite projective because it is a direct summand of the finite free module $R^{\oplus n}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module), line 2020: the lifted projector p and the conclusion 'Setting P = Im(p) we win'; the direct-sum calculation is written out here

proof.text: Apply $-\otimes_RS$ to the split decomposition in Step 1. The two inclusion and projection maps remain split after tensoring, so the canonical map $(\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS)\oplus(\operatorname{Im}(q)\otimes_RS)\to R^{\oplus n}\otimes_RS\cong S^{\oplus n}$ is an isomorphism; the induced map from the first summand is the map $v\otimes s\mapsto s\,\rho(v)$ by the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property]. Under this decomposition, the base-changed map $p\otimes1$ is the identity on $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS$ and zero on $\operatorname{Im}(q)\otimes_RS$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module), line 2020: the image of the lifted idempotent after reduction; tensoring the split projector decomposition is the explicit base-change argument

proof.text: The matrix of $p\otimes1$ in the base-changed standard basis is the entrywise image $\rho(X)$, so it is exactly $p_S$; in particular $p_S^2=p_S$. Since it is identity on the first summand and zero on the second, its image is precisely the first summand. Consequently the displayed map $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS\to S^{\oplus n}$ is injective and has image $\operatorname{Im}(p_S)$, and therefore identifies $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS$ with $\operatorname{Im}(p_S)$ as $S$-modules.

lean.statement: theorem idempotent_image_baseChange {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (p : Module.End R (Fin n → R)) (hp : IsIdempotentElem p) {S : Type v} [CommRing S] (ρ : R →+* S) : letI : Algebra R S := ρ.toAlgebra let pS : Module.End S (Fin n → S) := Matrix.toLin' ((LinearMap.toMatrix' p).map ρ) IsCompl p.range (1 - p).range ∧ (1 - p).range = p.ker ∧ Module.Finite R p.range ∧ Module.Projective R p.range ∧ IsIdempotentElem pS ∧ ∃ f : S ⊗[R] p.range →ₗ[S] (Fin n → S), (∀ (s : S) (x : p.range), f (s ⊗ₜ[R] x) = fun i ↦ s * ρ (x.val i)) ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ f.range = pS.range ∧ ∃ e : S ⊗[R] p.range ≃ₗ[S] pS.range, pS.range.subtype.comp e.toLinearMap = f
